clue.text: Roman general appears stupid to us

parts.note: crass means grossly stupid or insensitive
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone thinks a famous Roman commander looks dim.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus Licinius Crassus was a Roman military leader and member of the First Triumvirate with Caesar and Pompey.

clue.text: Critical point in Atlantic run, chaps

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Men on an Atlantic crossing reach a decisive moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'atlantiC RUN CHaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive moment or crisis is often called this informally.

clue.text: High land showing up on radar, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters of the preceding words are only one possible arrangement

explanation.surface: Mountains appearing as a blip on a radar screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges the letters of ON RADAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiny Pyrenean principality is a mountainous country.

clue.text: Deletes scores

explanation.surface: Crosses out marks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means crosses off a name or entry, and also means marks or grazes made on a surface.

clue.text: Nobody can be expected to wait for this

definitions.text: Nobody can be expected to wait for this

parts.words: Nobody can be expected to wait for this
parts.note: customers fetch their own food and goods, so staff never attend tables

explanation.surface: Something so slow that nobody should be expected to hang around for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wait' looks like hanging around; it means wait at table, as a waiter does.
explanation.definitionFit: In a shop or restaurant of this kind customers help themselves and no staff attend them.

clue.text: Sailor joining a vessel is a fool

parts.note: Jack (Jack Tar) is a traditional name for a sailor
SS stands for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: A seaman signing on to a ship turns out to be an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a male donkey, the word is a common insult for a stupid person.

clue.text: Flier in front of Jumbo, say

explanation.surface: An aircraft ahead of a jumbo jet.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter J, which stands in front of the rest of 'Jumbo', is pronounced this way.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a bird of the crow family, and also the spoken name of the tenth letter of the alphabet.

clue.text: Shaw copes with switch of directions

indicators.note: E and S are both compass directions, and switching them means one of them moves place

explanation.surface: The playwright Shaw manages with a change of stage directions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaw' is an old word for a small wood, not the playwright; swapping the compass letters E and S in COPES gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw is an archaic and dialect word for a thicket or small wood.

clue.text: US transport signal helps TV speaker

parts.note: auto is American for a car
a cue is a signal to begin speaking or acting

explanation.surface: An American car's indicator assists a television presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition describes what the device does rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: This screen device scrolls the script so a presenter can read it while facing the camera.

clue.text: Fish fit for a Poet Laureate

parts.note: a shad is a fish of the herring family
well means healthy, fit

explanation.surface: A fish fit to be served to the official national poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Shadwell held the post of the official royal poet after Dryden, who mocked him.

clue.text: Act subtly to exploit workers left inside

indicators.note: inside tells us the letter for left is placed within the word for exploiting workers

parts.note: to underpay staff is to exploit them

explanation.surface: Advice to a performer, oddly mixed with a remark about bosses exploiting staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts L within UNDERPAY, splitting it as UNDERP-L-AY.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a restrained, understated performance of a role is the theatre sense of the verb.

clue.text: Ancient city of Lancastrians, presumably

parts.note: Lancashire's emblem is the red rose, and Burgon's famous poem calls this Jordanian ruin 'a rose-red city half as old as time'

explanation.surface: A historian guesses at the ancient home of people from Lancaster.
explanation.walkthrough: The red rose is the emblem of the House of Lancaster and of Lancashire, an English county; the ruined city is famously 'rose-red', so the clue pretends it belongs to them.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruined Nabataean capital in Jordan is the 'rose-red city' of Burgon's poem, linking it to the red-rose county.

clue.text: Artist gets odd letters from 25

indicators.note: odd letters means the first, third, fifth and so on of the word that solves clue 25

parts.note: the solution to 25 across, the gallery where singers sit

explanation.surface: A painter picks up stray letters from a numbered source.
explanation.walkthrough: The number refers to another clue: take letters 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 of 25 across's solution.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Baptiste-Camille Corot was a French landscape painter of the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Accords we arranged make one immune to attack

indicators.note: arranged signals that the letters of the two words are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: Agreements we have drawn up make someone safe from attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' shuffles ACCORDS + WE.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or institution held to be beyond criticism is a revered thing nobody dares question.

clue.text: Music-lover has possibly gone? Correct

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of the two words may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a music fan has left, and is told yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges GONE + CORRECT.
explanation.definitionFit: One who attends performances of music in a hall is an enthusiast for it.

clue.text: Revolver blazing away in acrobat's turn

explanation.surface: A gun firing wildly during a circus performer's act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Revolver' suggests a gun, but here it is anything that spins.
explanation.definitionFit: The name covers both a spinning firework on a pin and, in gymnastics, a cartwheel.

clue.text: Hardened by exposure, came safely through

explanation.surface: Toughened by the elements, someone survived the ordeal.
explanation.definitionFit: It means worn or toughened by wind and rain, and also survived a storm or crisis.

clue.text: Avoids mountain route in some runs

indicators.note: in tells us the route through mountains goes inside the word for runs

parts.note: byes are runs in cricket scored without the batsman hitting the ball
a pass is a route through mountains

explanation.surface: A hiker skips the mountain path on some of their runs.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, byes are runs scored when the ball passes the batsman untouched; 'in' splits BYES as BY-PASS-ES.
explanation.definitionFit: To go round something rather than through it is to circumvent it.

clue.text: Royal house's employed porters in Northern tourist area

parts.note: York was an English royal house; with its 's this gives the word plus S
hired means taken on, employed
porter is a dark beer, so porters are ales

explanation.surface: A royal household's hired servants work in a northern holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'porters' looks like servants but means the dark beer.
explanation.definitionFit: The upland valleys of the English county in the north are a national park visited by many holidaymakers.

clue.text: Very wealthy revolutionary movement

explanation.surface: A rich man's political uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' suggests politics but means simply turning over and over.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling in money means extremely rich, and the word also describes turning over and over.

clue.text: Set off to trudge into river

indicators.note: into says the word for trudge goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
to plod is to walk heavily, to trudge

explanation.surface: Someone starts out by wading into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in south-west England; 'into' puts PLOD inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To set off a bomb is to detonate it, make it blow up.

clue.text: Stars put up with initial disapproval from audience

parts.note: boo is the sound a disapproving audience makes, here coming first

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word for put is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to set is to put

explanation.surface: Performers endure early jeers from the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stars' looks like performers, but it is a single constellation; 'up' in a down clue reads the word for put backwards beneath the jeer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Herdsman is a northern constellation containing the bright star Arcturus.

clue.text: Share in public plot

explanation.surface: Take part in a conspiracy in public.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain allotments are small plots of council land rented to the public for growing vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: It means a portion allocated to someone and also a rented vegetable patch on municipal land.

clue.text: The section of Yard that's cut crime

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: cut tells us the word for a section of a yard is shortened by losing its middle

parts.note: a foot is a third of a yard

explanation.surface: Part of Scotland Yard has been cut back, and crime results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard' suggests Scotland Yard, the London police headquarters, but it is the length; 'cut' trims FOOT to FT.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is the offence of taking another person's property.

clue.text: Thick-skinned type in place of Augustine

explanation.surface: An insensitive person living where a famous saint lived.
explanation.definitionFit: The short form names a large thick-hided African mammal, and Saint Augustine was bishop of the North African town of that name.

clue.text: Animals I spotted in all directions

indicators.note: spotted in says the letter is seen placed within the compass points

parts.note: the four compass points S, W, N and E

explanation.surface: Someone sees creatures everywhere they look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted in' puts I among the compass points, arranged as SW and NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigs are known collectively by this word, which is plural as well as singular.

clue.text: Voices raised here in the cathedral

definitions.text: Voices raised here in the cathedral

parts.words: Voices raised here in the cathedral
parts.note: the gallery of a cathedral where the singers stand, so their voices are literally raised above the floor

explanation.surface: Sounds of protest are heard in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Voices raised' suggests protest; here the singers are physically high up.
explanation.definitionFit: This raised gallery in a church is where the singers perform.

clue.text: Fish caught round Land's End

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
O is round in shape

indicators.note: End points to the last letter of the word Land

explanation.surface: A fish landed off the tip of Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: Land's End is the far south-western tip of England; here it just gives the last letter of Land.
explanation.definitionFit: A common white-fleshed sea fish of the North Atlantic.

clue.text: Located and summoned, say, and seen

indicators.note: say signals that we want a word pronounced like the one for summoned

parts.note: cited means summoned to appear in court

explanation.surface: A witness is found, called to court and spotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Located' also works as a sound-alike, since SITED sounds the same, giving three senses in all.
explanation.definitionFit: To have caught sight of something is to have spotted it.

clue.text: Correct to change into second gear?

explanation.surface: A driving instructor tells a learner to shift up a gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gear' is clothing, not a car's gears: to re-dress is to dress again in a second outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: To set right a wrong is to remedy it; split as re-dress it means putting on clothes again.
